title: Check if the Sentence Is Pangram
statement: A pangram is text in which each of the 26 lowercase English letters shows up one or more times. The string `sentence` is made only of lowercase English letters. Return `true` when `sentence` is a pangram and `false` when at least one letter of the alphabet never occurs in it.
constraints: sentence contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The question is only whether every letter appears somewhere, so we need to remember which distinct letters we have met. A set does exactly that, and its size tells us how many different letters we have. The moment the set holds 26 letters, the answer is settled. The brute-force idea scans the whole string once per alphabet letter, which is 26 passes instead of one.

## Approach

1. Create an empty set `seen`.
2. Walk through `sentence` one `letter` at a time and add it to `seen` (adding a repeat changes nothing).
3. After each addition, if `seen.size` is 26, every letter has appeared, so return `true` right away.
4. If the loop ends without reaching 26 distinct letters, some letter is missing: return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`sentence = "thequickbrownfoxjumpsoverthelazydog"`. The set grows with `t, h, e, q, u, i, c, k, b, r, o, w, n, f, x, j, m, p, s`; letters such as the second `o` or `u` are already present and change nothing. Then `v` (20), `l` (21), `a` (22), `z` (23), `y` (24), `d` (25) and finally `g` makes 26, so the function returns `true`. For `"leetcode"` the set ends with only 5 letters, so the answer is `false`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is added to the set once, in constant time.
- Space: O(1): the set never holds more than 26 letters.

## Pitfalls

- Strings shorter than 26 characters can never be pangrams; the set check handles this without a special case.
- Count distinct letters, not characters: `sentence.length >= 26` proves nothing.
- Do not stop at the first repeated letter; repeats are allowed and simply ignored.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | set of distinct letters met so far |
| `letter` | the current character of `sentence` |

narration.2: Create an empty set to hold the distinct letters we have met.
narration.4: Visit the sentence one letter at a time.
narration.5: Record the letter; adding one that is already present changes nothing.
narration.6: Once 26 distinct letters are stored, the whole alphabet has appeared.
narration.7: So the sentence is a pangram and we can stop early.
narration.10: The loop finished without collecting all 26 letters, so at least one is missing.
